items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: Louie Belson left the band, Louie had followed Buddy Rich.

ctx.x: two $20 bills, and waved them at the band and grinned, and stopped the show for about 5 minutes, chuckling at his winning the bet.

After that three weeks with Tom Dorsey, I didn't work with him again, that I can recall, until 1958, and the incidents that happened then -- I was doing the Hit Parade then, and Tom had been having -- had a fight with Louie Belson. Louie Belson left the band, Louie had followed Buddy Rich. Charlie Shavers was still with him, and they were at the Pennsylvania Hotel.

Well, he wanted to sign me to a contract as Louie Belson said he wasn't coming back -- but I couldn't afford, I was doing so well on the outside, and those were the top years for me -- being a musician on the outside and then the studios -- and I couldn't afford it, I had built my new home here in Whitestone, New York, and I didn't want any road travel. I wanted to continue doing what I was doing. So I refused.
